class.name: PhysX
class.brief_description: Script queries about the PhysX physics backend.
class.description: Static queries about the PhysX backend as a whole, for a game that adapts to the machine it runs on, e.g. choosing [PhysXParticleFluid3D]'s solver or how much debris to spawn: [codeblock] if PhysX.is_gpu_available(): print("GPU physics on ", PhysX.get_gpu_device_name()) [/codeblock]

method.name: get_gpu_device_name
method.description: Returns the name of the CUDA device GPU dynamics runs on (for example [code]"NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070"[/code]), or an empty string when [method is_gpu_available] is [code]false[/code].

method.name: is_gpu_available
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when PhysX is the active physics engine and is running GPU dynamics on a CUDA device. It is [code]false[/code] in a build without GPU support, on a machine without a usable NVIDIA GPU or without [code]PhysXGpu[/code] shipped next to the executable, with [code]physics/physx_3d/simulation/enhanced_determinism[/code] on or [code]physics/physx_3d/simulation/gpu_dynamics[/code] off, or when another physics engine is selected. Without it, GPU-only features fall back or stay inert: [PhysXParticleFluid3D] with the PBD solver, GPU cloth and so on. Valid once the physics server has started (from any node's [code]_ready[/code] on).
